gaps.sentence: ___ single room in the hotel was fully booked.
gaps.explanation: 'Every single room' is the emphatic collocation meaning 'without exception'.

gaps.sentence: ___ of what he says is nonsense.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of what he says' is the pattern 'most of + noun clause'; 'the most of' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: I asked ___ in the office, but nobody knew the answer.
gaps.explanation: 'I asked everybody' (all the people) contrasts with 'nobody knew'; 'everything' refers to things, not people.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ interruptions this year, so the ceremony ran far more smoothly.
We had ___ luggage that the taxi couldn't take it all.
gaps.explanation: 'So much luggage that …' — luggage is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the equipment has been serviced this year, so breakdowns are rare.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of + noun' = the majority of it; 'the most' is a superlative.

gaps.sentence: We haven't received ___ information about the delay.
gaps.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so 'much' is required in the negative sentence.

gaps.sentence: Very ___ applicants had the required experience.
gaps.hint: 'very' + negative quantifier with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Very few' means almost none and is used with countables; 'very a few' is impossible.
